name: cmdgate-vscode
description: A second opinion on the shell commands an AI agent asks you to approve: dangerous, root access, risk level and safe/unsafe, from your locally running Command Gate app.

cmdgate.endpoint.description: Decision API endpoint of the locally running Command Gate app.

cmdgate.model.description: Value sent as `model` in each request (use it to pick one of the app's models).

cmdgate.timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the app before showing 'no answer'.

cmdgate.threshold.description: Probability at or above which a yes/no answer is shown as 'yes' (dangerous, root, unsafe).

dangerous.instructions: Could this shell command cause serious damage, data loss or a security problem if it runs as written?

requires_root.instructions: Does this shell command need root or administrator privileges to run?

risk_level.instructions: How much damage could this shell command do if it runs as written?
criteria: safe: read-only or routine, no plausible path to data loss, privilege change or disruption
low: a local change that is quick to undo
moderate: repairable without backups, with some effort
high: needs backups to recover, exposes secrets to others, runs unverified code, or takes the machine down
critical: destroys a disk, filesystem, system directory or home folder, or gives away root-level control

unsafe.instructions: Should a person approve this shell command before an AI coding agent runs it?

cmdgate.questions.description: Questions sent with each command, in decision API format. Change IDs or wording to match what the app was trained on.

cmdgate.fields.description: Which question ID fills each field on screen.

cmdgate.showCard.description: Open the second-opinion card beside the editor (without taking focus) when a command is checked.

cmdgate.chatCardPort.description: Experimental. 0 = off. When set, serves the latest result for a command on 127.0.0.1:<port>/card, readable only by VS Code webviews, so a patched chat view can show the card inline. Reload the window after changing it.

cmdgate.notifyOnPrompt.description: Also show VS Code's plain notification toast for permission prompts: always, flagged only, or off.
